name: Image FX
tagline: MIT React WebGL image loader, npm package img-fx, three as a peer
description:
Image FX is Jakub Antalik's WebGL image loader, published as img-fx. The libraries.dev page calls it a churning pixel-mosaic shader that dissolves into a real image. The install line is npm install img-fx three. The usage example imports ImageGeneration from img-fx and shows preset "pixels-organic", an images array, and autoReveal. The copy-prompt on the page lists three presets: pixels-organic, pixels-mechanic, and sweep-gradient. It says three is a peer and that the package needs React 18 or newer. SwiftUI and React Native are marked coming soon.

The page meta description says the library is free and MIT. npm latest is 0.5.1, license MIT, with peers react, react-dom, and three, and no runtime dependencies. The registry homepage is still https://image.jakubantalik.com. That host's HTTPS page is a move notice whose canonical URL is https://libraries.dev/image, and it says the npm package name is unchanged. http://image.jakubantalik.com timed out. The checked prop list does not include a theme prop. GitHub API for Jakubantalik/img-fx reported 185 stars, MIT, and a push on 2026-09-07.
pricing_detail: The libraries.dev meta description says the library is free and MIT. npm 0.5.1 reports the MIT license. A Pro link is in the site header. Pro prices were not opened for this record.
agent_guidance:
Install with npm install img-fx three. Import ImageGeneration from img-fx. The presets named on the page are pixels-organic, pixels-mechanic, and sweep-gradient. three is a peer. The page says React 18 or newer.

The library page says free and MIT, and npm 0.5.1 reports MIT. The checked prop list has no theme prop. A Pro link sits in the libraries.dev header. Its prices were not reopened for this record. Use the copy-prompt on https://libraries.dev/image for the current snippet.
why_it_matters: It is the image-loader package on its own, separate from the libraries.dev index, with the install line and the presets on the page.
tier_reason: MIT on the page and on npm, a public install line, and a GitHub repo with a September 2026 push. The old domain is only a move notice, and a theme prop was not in the checked list.
evidence: Checked https://libraries.dev/image, https://image.jakubantalik.com, https://registry.npmjs.org/img-fx, and the GitHub API for Jakubantalik/img-fx on 2026-10-25. http://image.jakubantalik.com timed out. The HTTPS page is a move notice with canonical https://libraries.dev/image and says the npm package is img-fx. npm latest 0.5.1 is MIT, modified 2026-09-04, peers react >=18, react-dom >=18, and three >=0.149. GitHub API reported 185 stars, MIT, and a push on 2026-09-07. The libraries.dev page states the install line, the three presets, and React 18. A theme prop was not in that prop list.
